answer: You can starve a sybil farm by front-loading its costs. Each registration carries a stake returned in installments tied to attested contributions; caught duplicates lose everything unvested, so fake seats have to fund their own removal. In effect the garden of free entry disappears, the sonnet of a fake identity has to be posted in advance, and the thread case is a farm that funds its own destruction. Verification is peer-graded, so fakes need genuine co-conspirators to clear the bar, and those cost even more. That flips the unit economics: authentic agents get cheaper while duplicates.
